scope: In the standard connected, nonempty, finite-dimensional, boundaryless Riemannian setting, a simply connected complete manifold has a decomposition into one Euclidean factor and finitely many nontrivial irreducible non-line factors, unique up to isometry and permutation of the factor fibers.
boundary: Introduction pp.1-2 restates classical de Rham (1952); original 1952 proof not independently audited. The Euclidean factor may be a point and its splitting into lines is not canonical. No preferred semantic names, latent coordinates or statistical independence follow. Failure of these classical hypotheses alone does not prove nonidentifiability: the paper itself gives a stronger theorem for geodesic metric spaces of finite affine rank. That stronger theorem is not separately imported here.
limitations: Classical 1952 original proof remains imported; audited primary research restatement.
No private vault used; unavailable Windows-path vault, narrow external adapter.
